assessments.reasoning: json/details/OSL-2.0.json gives OSL-2.0, “Open Software License 2.0” and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Both reference fields cite http://web.archive.org/web/20041020171434/http://www.rosenlaw.com/osl2.0.html.
The SPDX repository’s unsigned v3.29.0 annotated tag targets the commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48 used by the 2.0 detail URL.
The OSI .txt snapshot opens with v. 2.0 and the same edition-specific application notice as SPDX’s standardLicenseHeader. This establishes publisher context directly from the text.

In the November 7, 2003 OSI list archive, Rosen names the Open Software License and immediately cites http://opensource.org/licenses/osl-2.0.php. The thread’s “For Approval” subject concerns HAL and supplies no OSL board decision.

challenge.method: Compared the commit and detail fields, then distinguished the cited author HTML, the archived OSI .txt and the OSI .php cited in the HAL thread. Checked SPDX’s recorded link status.
challenge.results: The author HTML reference is marked isValid=false and isLive=false. The pinned detail itself gives the ID and 2.0 notice. OSI’s plaintext confirms that edition, and the 2003 message identifies another historical route without proving a byte match, compatibility or approval.

limitations: The scheduled evidence includes the SPDX citation to archived Rosen HTML, the OSI plaintext and Rosen’s message. The target HTML bodies of the Rosen URL and OSI PHP URL were not inspected. Their contents and legal equivalence remain unverified.
reasoning: SPDX’s pinned detail and OSI’s archived plaintext identify the same named 2.0 edition in their notices. Rosen’s contemporaneous reference also associates the Open Software License with an OSI 2.0 publication route.
